projects.title: Clinic Queue Manager
projects.summary: A queue management prototype that gives clinic staff a clear view of patient flow during busy hours.
projects.role: Backend developer · data structures and algorithms
projects.problem: Paper lists and ad hoc updates make it difficult for a small clinic team to keep an accurate order when arrivals bunch together or urgent cases need attention.
projects.approach: Modeled arrivals as explicit queue entries, then separated standard FIFO handling from priority insertions. Kept the operations small and measurable so each data structure choice could be reasoned about and tested.
projects.outcome: Built a lightweight C++ prototype around an explicit queue model, with operations for check-in, priority handling, lookup, and completion. The project focused on predictable behavior and clear complexity trade-offs.
projects.metric: Placeholder metric to replace after testing: target 20% shorter average wait time.

cover.alt: Queue dashboard concept showing patient sequence, wait time, and priority status

projects.title: Social Media Agent
projects.summary: An AI-assisted workflow for turning a brief into a reviewed, platform-ready draft using the Gemini API.
projects.problem: Preparing a consistent set of social drafts from a short campaign brief often means repeating the same research, formatting, and review work across channels.
projects.approach: Turned the brief into a validated structured input, asked the Gemini API for bounded draft options, then returned a typed response into a human review queue. Kept publishing outside the prototype so generated content could not be posted without approval.
projects.outcome: Prototyped an agent workflow that accepts a brief, produces structured draft options, and leaves a human review step before anything can be published. Input and output shapes are validated so incomplete results are easy to catch.
projects.metric: Placeholder evaluation to replace: compare review time across 10 representative briefs.

cover.alt: Campaign workspace concept with a brief and three reviewed draft options

notes.title: Make the human review step part of the design
notes.excerpt: A useful AI workflow makes it easy to inspect, correct, and trust the work before it moves forward.
notes.body:
Automation is most helpful when it reduces repeated effort without making decisions invisible. In the Social Media Agent prototype, generated drafts remain drafts: people can inspect structure, adjust tone, and choose what moves forward. That review step is part of the product, not a patch added at the end.

The same principle applies to internal tools. Make state visible, give people a clear way to correct mistakes, and measure the work that matters before claiming a result.
